sections.title: Market Pulse: AI Selloff Drags Down Tech on Friday

items.headline: U.S. Markets Conclude Week with Significant Declines for Tech, Amid AI Financing Concerns and Rising Oil Prices
items.summary: U.S. stock markets experienced notable declines on Friday, October 17, primarily driven by concerns over artificial intelligence financing, high borrowing costs, and rising oil prices. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite bore the brunt of the selloff, recording its worst weekly performance since June. A clear rotation from growth and AI-related stocks into more defensive and value-oriented sectors was observed.

items.headline: Technology and Semiconductor Sectors Face Significant Pressure
items.summary: The technology sector, particularly semiconductors, endured heavy losses on Friday. Chipmakers like $AMD (-6%), $INTC (-5.8%), $MU (-5.6%), and $AVGO (-4.5%) were hit hard, contributing to the Nasdaq's sharp decline. Concerns over AI financing and potential overvaluation of AI-related infrastructure investments were key drivers.

items.headline: Shift to Value and Defensive Stocks Evident
items.summary: Investors rotated out of growth and AI stocks into value and defensive sectors, including consumer staples and utilities. Companies like $T-Mobile US (+1.32%), $KDP (+1.29%), $COST (+1.13%), and $ADP (+1.14%) saw gains, indicating a flight to businesses with stable cash flow in a high-interest rate environment.

items.headline: Sticky Inflation and Fed Rate Hike Expectations Persist
items.summary: Hotter-than-expected CPI and PPI data reinforced inflation concerns, primarily fueled by rising energy prices. Despite some volatility, the market still anticipates a high probability (around 74.3%) of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, with the 10-year Treasury yield settling around 5.09% on Friday.

items.headline: Oil Prices Remain Elevated, Fueling Economic Slowdown Fears
items.summary: Crude oil prices, now above $100, have climbed over 70% year-to-date, largely due to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. These persistently high energy costs are contributing to inflation and are seen as a potential drag on economic growth.

items.headline: IMF and World Bank Meetings Highlight Global Economic Challenges
items.summary: Leaders at the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok discussed a challenging global economic outlook, citing the war in Iran driving fuel prices and inflation, soaring public debt, and the crucial but regionally uneven role of AI investments.

items.headline: Mixed Earnings Reports Influence Individual Stock Movements
items.summary: Blackbaud ($BLKB) climbed 9% after reporting an earnings beat, while DigitalOcean ($DOCN) dropped 11% on lowered guidance. Morgan Stanley's Q3 earnings exceeded expectations, though its stock underperformed, and Citigroup's Q3 results, while beating estimates, showed sequential declines.
